analysis:
Documentation-only PR. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md line 141 changes the reconnect-backoff reference from ExponentialBackoff in CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md adds a section (head lines 202-219) describing that the provider reads the WebSocket close code from the coordinator side. Code 1012 draws a wait from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff. Any other code or no close frame uses the next ExponentialBackoff range. A session open for stableSessionDuration or longer, counted from its register frame, resets the backoff. Every reconnect sends a fresh register.

Security relevance (TB-002, TB-011, T-053, T-057): no code, auth, crypto, or trust-policy change is made. The new text says the close code is the only input used and the close reason is ignored. The coordinator is trusted, so a 1012 can only shorten or stabilize reconnect delay. It cannot grant serving authorization, and the doc states fresh registration, which is consistent with T-053's per-connection binding. A DoS angle (a hostile or MITM peer sending 1012 to keep the wait short) would only produce bounded reconnect load. The wait is drawn from a range, and TLS to the coordinator is assumed. No threat-model assumption is invalidated.

Unverified: the actual behavior of CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, its constants, and whether the "older providers treat 1012 like any other close" claim holds are outside the supplied evidence, since the Swift source is not included. Recommend a consistency check against the source if the docs are to be trusted. This is a doc-accuracy question, not a vulnerability. The troubleshooting.md and protocol-messages.md units were read in full; the content outside the changed lines is unchanged context.
